decisive_items: well‐defined hyperpigmented, hyperkeratotic plaques with thick adherent scales and a peripheral rim of erythema distributed symmetrically over the dorsum of both feet and around the knees
hyperkeratosis, parakeratosis, focal subcorneal clefting with keratinocyte necrosis
Plasma zinc was at the lower end of normal (72 μg/dL; reference range 70–120 μg/dL)
response.rationale: The acral distribution, rimmed hyperkeratotic plaques, and biopsy showing subcorneal clefting with keratinocyte necrosis are characteristic of a necrolytic/zinc-deficiency dermatosis. Borderline zinc and negative hepatitis serologies support zinc deficiency over psoriasis, which would not explain keratinocyte necrosis; hypothyroidism does not match the biopsy findings.

rejected.why: Psoriasis explains hyperkeratosis, parakeratosis, and plaques, but the focal subcorneal clefting with keratinocyte necrosis and acral rimmed morphology are atypical, and the borderline zinc is not addressed.
Hypothyroidism is supported only by elevated TSH; it does not explain the specific plaque morphology or the biopsy findings of subcorneal clefting and keratinocyte necrosis.
